overall_assessment:
Verdict: not accepted as a clean test-quality gate. The composed evidence is honest and materially useful, but two material contract-boundary gaps remain; one is a production parsing/classification defect.

Framing: this review covers the frozen nine public paths bound by cp36e-source-after.sha256, including the current Meta adapter unit suite, Nest/BFF plus real PostgreSQL E2E surface, Evolution convergence, and the immutable reused Web/browser evidence. It does not accept real Meta/OAuth/device recovery, operator IN/OUT proof, Railway/runtime health, or external delivery.

Evidence reviewed: cp36e-tqa-package.md; current source and named-path diffs; cp36e source manifests; cp36d and cp36e validation receipts and targeted raw-log evidence. The current API leaf reports lint, build, 141 unit tests, 288 PostgreSQL E2E tests, and 22 migrations passing. Web 28 and browser 47 are correctly represented only as immutable cp36d reuse because the eight relevant production/fixture/Web paths are byte-identical; this is not a new all-suite, browser, or preworker claim.

Five audit questions:
1. Does each changed behavior have an effective test? Mostly. Meta paging, typed unavailability, receipt convergence, stale fencing, and Web invite selection are exercised. Successful malformed or structurally invalid Meta payloads are not.
2. Does each relevant test exercise the intended production boundary? Yes for the adapter unit tests, and substantially yes for BFF/real PostgreSQL/browser layers. The unit suite instantiates the real MetaHttpClient; BFF E2E uses the real application/controller/session/CSRF/Prisma path with the port overridden; browser imports the actual built production error constructor and token.
3. Would the tests fail for plausible regressions? For bounded pages, error-class/code, exact receipt convergence, and invite POST success, generally yes. They would not fail if a malformed successful Graph response became a false absence, nor if the BFF safe-text/selective-error-mapping contract regressed while status/catalog code remained unchanged.
4. Is test cost proportionate and efficient? Yes. The adapter verifies the actual HTTP construction with bounded fetch doubles; the BFF suite uses one disposable PostgreSQL environment; browser evidence is reused only where immutable hashes justify it. The verifier itself remains bounded to one debug request plus at most two page requests under the lease budget. No fresh performance/SLO measurement was supplied.
5. Are results trustworthy across build/platform/decision boundaries? Partly. The Windows Docker Node 22/OpenSSL 3/PostgreSQL evidence, fresh API build, real-PG E2E, and source-hash composition are sound. Browser/Web reuse is provenance-correct but not fresh. Real external/provider/runtime proof remains explicitly blocked.

Bypass and failure-mode review: no focused/skipped tests, retry/sleep acceptance, production mock fallback, or test-only route was found in the reviewed paths. The browser fixture overrides the same production META_CLIENT token and uses symbols imported from the built module, so it does not counterfeit error-class identity. However, response.json().catch(() => ({})) is a silent parse fallback that converts some successful-but-invalid provider responses into conclusive absence; this is an efficacy failure rather than an allowed resilience path.

Fail-first assessment: the cp36d typed-error BFF boundary has credible prior RED evidence, with the old path returning 500/no catalog code before the mapper repair. The cp36e class-plus-code changes are assertion strengthening after the production fix, not independently demonstrated REDs; that is acceptable only as such. The Web fixture-selection change is a legitimate precondition repair, not evidence of a product loading-race fix.

DI, real-PG, CI/platform/build: DI parity is strong for the declared layers. The browser server imports META_CLIENT and MetaIndisponivelError from production dist; BFF tests use the same injection token with a controlled external-port fake; the actual adapter is separately tested. The PostgreSQL E2E receipt is real database evidence, not an in-memory substitute. Build evidence is valid for the current API leaf; the current spec is excluded from production dist, preserving the reused browser-bundle premise. Canonical CI-equivalent evidence is local Windows Docker evidence, not a claim of hosted CI or external runtime completion.

Decision adherence matrix: D-01 BU canonical: adherent. D-02 verified provider boundary: adherent within local adapter/BFF scope. D-03 exact owner/attempt/generation/epoch/receipt fencing: adherent. D-04 scoped credential/no global fallback: adherent. D-05 official verification/error boundary: source is substantially adherent, but test contract coverage is incomplete. D-06 real Evolution/device recovery proof: exception, still external/runtime pending. D-07 bounded observation/absence semantics: exception because invalid successful provider payload can become null. D-08 caller scope: adherent in reviewed BFF evidence. D-09 local runner: adherent. D-10 principal serialized validation: adherent.

Uncertainty matrix: confirmed—current API leaf, bounded adapter request behavior, real-PG BFF behavior, exact-state convergence, and immutable reuse composition. Reused but not rerun—Web unit 28 and Chromium browser 47 from cp36d. Not measured—throughput, SLOs, and fresh browser execution under cp36e. Blocked/out of scope—real Meta/OAuth/device/provider calls, human recovery proof, Railway/runtime deployment and continuous health. No conclusion here waives those delivery gates.
recommended_path: Resolve TQA-CP36E-01 before acceptance: make malformed JSON and missing/non-array page data fail closed as the typed temporary-unavailability path rather than conclusive absence; add focused real-MetaHttpClient tests for malformed JSON, missing data, and non-array data, then prove the BFF result is the safe 503 boundary. Resolve TQA-CP36E-02 with BFF contract assertions for the exact safe public message/no provider leakage and a generic non-Meta error that is not remapped to META_INDISPONIVEL. After any source or test change, create a new freeze/receipt and rerun the canonical API leaf; rerun Web/browser only if their frozen bytes or affected build/runtime inputs change. Obtain a fresh independent TQA and separate final review after the repaired receipt. Keep D-06/VAL-05 external provider/device/runtime evidence explicitly pending; this audit must not promote whole-runtime or external delivery.

findings.title: Malformed successful Meta page can be classified as conclusive absence
findings.rationale: Issue card. Evidence: api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts parses a successful response with response.json().catch(() => ({})); numerosDaWaba then treats absent data as an empty terminal page, and verificarNumeroVinculado returns null. The service consequently follows its ordinary resource-not-found path rather than the required typed safe 503 path. This violates the frozen rule that null means only exhaustively observed absence; parse/shape/contract failures must fail loudly. Current meta.client.spec.ts covers bounded pages, invalid grant, budget, cycle, and oversized cursor, but not malformed JSON, missing data, or non-array data. Option A, leave it unchanged, retains false absence and is not acceptable. Option B, add only a test, demonstrates but does not repair the defect. Option C, recommended, fail closed in the adapter and cover adapter plus BFF boundary behavior.
findings.suggested_action: Validate successful provider payload shape before interpreting it: malformed JSON, missing data, and non-array data must raise MetaIndisponivelError. Add real MetaHttpClient unit cases and a BFF/real-PG assertion that the resulting public response is 503 META_INDISPONIVEL while durable state and the owned lease remain safe. Regenerate the frozen receipt and rerun the API CI-equivalent leaf.

findings.title: BFF error-boundary tests do not fully lock the safe envelope or selective mapping
findings.rationale: Issue card. The current BFF E2E asserts 503 and catalogCode for MetaIndisponivelError, and source currently maps only that class. It does not assert the mandated fixed safe public text/no raw provider detail, nor prove that an arbitrary non-Meta exception remains unremapped. A broad catch or changed message could therefore pass the current test while breaking the frozen error-boundary contract. Option A, rely on source inspection, leaves a regression hole. Option B, change production behavior without a test, is unnecessary because the present source is correct. Option C, recommended, add BFF assertions only.
findings.suggested_action: Extend the existing BFF/real-PostgreSQL error case to assert the exact fixed public message and absence of provider detail. Add a generic port-error case proving it is not translated into META_INDISPONIVEL, while preserving the existing state/credential/identity/audit/lease assertions.
